t: Reference Manager - public implementations survey
title: Reference Manager - public implementations survey
definition: Organizes research sources and bibliographic information.
description:
This database surveys Reference Manager as it exists in public practice: Organizes research sources and bibliographic information. The records below name real tools with real track records, explain the techniques they are built on, cite the standards they implement, and provide drills that build working skill. Nothing here is speculative - every implementation is a real project you can download, every technique is established practice.

The value of a survey like this is comparative: seeing seven real implementations side by side reveals what the capability truly requires and where each tool draws its boundaries. The technique records go deeper, explaining the machinery - the algorithms, protocols and disciplines - that make Reference Manager work regardless of which tool you pick.

Use this database as a field guide. When a build calls for Reference Manager, consult the spotlights to choose an implementation, check the standards to stay interoperable, and run the drills to build fluency. Each record's demo program runs with node - the capability is demonstrated end to end.

t: Reference Manager handoff protocol - practitioner discipline
title: Reference Manager handoff protocol - practitioner discipline
definition: The handoff protocol discipline for Reference Manager: organizes research sources and bibliographic information..
description:
Good Reference Manager practice is not talent - it is handoff protocol. It turns Reference Manager from an event into a repeatable capability.

Concretely: run the smallest meaningful case first and verify it by hand; log every decision with its reason, so the next builder inherits understanding; verify outputs against the original request, not against your hopes This record exists because the difference between a tool and a capability is discipline. Run the demo, adopt the checklist, and Reference Manager becomes something your builds can rely on.

t: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Reference Manager
title: Foundation drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Reference Manager
definition: Ladder drill (foundation): name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Reference Manager from a one-paragraph brief.
description:
FOUNDATION drill - name the inputs, outputs, and contracts of Reference Manager from a one-paragraph brief. Read the brief twice. List every input the Reference Manager needs, every output it must produce, and one contract each input-output pair must satisfy.

The attached program executes a reference solution step by step; run it with node, then re-run it with changed inputs to test your understanding. The drill is complete when you can list them from memory without looking at the brief

t: Foundation drill - label the seven pillars of the Signature Reference Manager o
title: Foundation drill - label the seven pillars of the Signature Reference Manager o
definition: Ladder drill (foundation): label the seven pillars of the Signature Reference Manager on a blank diagram.
description:
Drill (FOUNDATION): label the seven pillars of the Signature Reference Manager on a blank diagram

Draw seven boxes. Name each pillar of the Reference Manager framework and write its one-line responsibility under it, in your own words. Work it by hand first, then run the demo program and compare its trace against your own reasoning. When they agree, the concept is yours.

Success criterion: another builder agrees your labels match the framework
